content: A vulnerability in KVM, the Linux hypervisor, lets guest VMs access host memory on AMD-hosted servers. This affects DigitalOcean shared servers with nested virtualization. The flaw, CVE-2026-99312, was exploited to read about 127 GB of memory. Mitigation involves updating to fixed kernels.

Security leaders are increasing the autonomy of AI agents in low-risk security actions. By 2027, 60% expect to be comfortable with autonomous AI. The shift aims to enhance efficiency in Security Operations Centers (SOC).
title: AI Autonomy in Security Operations
UK Court Forces Government to Admit Demanding Apple iCloud Backdoor
content: The UK Investigatory Powers Tribunal confirmed the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data. Apple’s decision to revoke Advanced Data Protection for UK users was seen as indirect confirmation. The government argues it is necessary for national security, but Apple opposes, emphasizing customer privacy. A substantive hearing is scheduled for 2027.

title: BYOD Ransomware Hackers Play Audio Ransom Messages on Computers Across Hospitals and Universities
content: Ransomware hackers used audio messages to demand ransom from multiple institutions, causing operational disruptions. The University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center and Vanderbilt University experienced audio demands, with the latter ordering a device shutdown. BYOD claimed to have compromised 36,000 systems and stole over a million Social Security numbers. Victims faced unexpected login prompts and credential compromises. Mitigation includes checking logs, testing backups, and reporting unsolicited messages.

title: Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX Framework to Automate Cyberattacks Without Relying on Zero-Day Exploits
content: Attackers are using an AI-driven testing tool called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks by finding and exploiting ordinary mistakes in company networks. This tool has been used by criminals and state-linked groups since at least August 2026. It can reach privileged access in under three hours. Defenders should limit exposed APIs, set WAF rules, and use disposable VMs for testing to mitigate risks.

A vulnerability in Windows 11 passkey authentication can trigger error messages on Android devices even after a successful sign-in. A fix has been released for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. The issue impacts cross-device authentication using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager. Until patched, users can ignore errors if authentication succeeds on the PC.
title: Windows 11 passkey bug causes authentication failure messages
SonicWall Urges Replacement of Gen 6 Firewalls Due to Security Risks
content: SonicWall advises retiring Generation 6 firewalls due to security risks from AI-assisted attacks. Customers are urged to replace and stop exposing these devices on the internet to mitigate vulnerabilities. Technical impact includes increased risk of exploitation by attackers using automation and AI.

Threat actors exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway, to breach a Russian organization. The breach involved four devices and provided access to the internal network. CVSS score: 9.8.
title: Hackers Exploit Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw, Breach Four Devices and Reach Internal Network
No Straight Lines: The value of a different career journey
content: No straight lines: career changes, breaks, and diverse industry experience build resilience, curiosity, and perspective. Communities support career transitions, recognizing transferable skills. Diverse journeys strengthen inclusive teams in tech.

title: BADBOX 3.0 malware used Android TV boxes for ad fraud
content: BADBOX 3.0 malware compromised Android TV boxes to generate 40 billion daily bid requests for ad fraud. This affected homeowners whose internet connections were sold for advertising. The technical impact included unauthorized use of devices for hidden video ads and increased advertiser competition. Mitigation involved disrupting the operation.

Signal is restricting screenshots on iOS 27 and some Android devices to prevent AI assistants from reading private chats. The change targets Apple’s Siri and Google Gemini, addressing the risk of AI assistants capturing message text post-delivery. Users can turn off the protection in privacy settings but exposing messages to other people in the chat is a risk.
title: Signal Restricts Screenshots to Protect User Privacy from AI Assistants
UK tribunal confirms secret Apple order in iCloud encryption dispute
content: The UK’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal confirmed a secret order from the Home Office to Apple for access to encrypted iCloud data. This decision rejects the government’s attempt to keep the order secret, highlighting potential cybersecurity and privacy risks.

title: Empowering Employees to Make a Difference: The Digital Café
content: The Digital Café helps the Nauheim community build technology confidence. Sophos volunteers provide 40 hours of paid leave for the initiative, enhancing digital inclusion. No technical impact or mitigation details available.

A critical Java vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) affects Palo Alto Networks products, enabling remote code execution under specific conditions. Affected products include Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector, and on-premises HTML5 Gateway. Customers should upgrade to the latest versions. The vulnerability is rated CVSS 9.2 and requires Java running on x86-64 processors with AVX-512 VBMI support and specific configurations.
title: Palo Alto Confirms Critical Java Vulnerability Affects Privilege Threat Analytics and Remote Access Connector

content: ClamAV released versions 1.5.5 and 1.4.7 to address 10 high-severity vulnerabilities that could crash antivirus scanners, cause endless loops, or drain system resources. Affected components include email handling, document parsing, and archive extraction. Attackers could exploit these flaws to disrupt scanning availability or gain unauthorized access. Administrators should update to the latest versions to mitigate these risks.
title: ClamAV Patches 10 High-Severity Vulnerabilities That Could Let Attackers Crash Antivirus Scanners

content: Transport for London (TfL) detected a breach on its Oyster photocard website, exposing personal information of 265,000 customers, including email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth. TfL advised customers to change matching passwords or security answers used on other accounts. The breach did not compromise passwords, bank details, or payment card information.
title: Hackers Breach TfL Oyster Photocard Accounts, Exposing Personal Data of 265,000 Customers

content: Hackers exploited misconfigured Temenos Quantum Fabric to deploy web shells without passwords, gaining admin access via a misconfigured authentication service. Affected financial institutions across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The exploit used custom Java integrations to gain access to application and database connections. Defenders should check for unexpected Java packages and service imports, and log suspicious activities.
title: Hackers Exploit Misconfigured Temenos Banking Platform to Deploy Web Shells Without Passwords
Chase says vendor cyberattack may have exposed customer data
content: Attackers targeted third-party vendors, potentially exposing customer names and email addresses. Chase, Visa, and Mastercard disclosed incidents after data was stolen and posted online. Mitigation involves monitoring and tightening vendor security.

title: AI's Mathematical Advances Spark Debate on Public-Key Cryptography Security
content: A cryptographer warns that existing public-key cryptography systems may fail due to AI advancements, posing a threat to PKI. Experts debate the need for immediate action or gradual modernization. The main concern is that AI could find shortcuts to solving hard mathematical problems underlying PKI. While some suggest cautious improvement, others recommend following established modernization paths.

Attackers are scanning LiteLLM servers for two vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710) to gain remote code execution (RCE) without authentication. The first flaw allows execution of commands with the proxy’s privileges, while the second bypasses login checks. Exploits target the /mcp-rest/test/tools/list path and use crafted Host headers. Affected servers can expose API keys and cloud access. Mitigation includes patching and restricting public access. Teams should rotate keys and review logs for suspicious activity.
title: Hackers Actively Scan LiteLLM AI Servers for Critical Flaws Enabling RCE Attacks
ROMULUS ClickFix Attacks Deliver RAT That Can Spy on Users and Control PCs
content: Threat actors use ROMULUS ClickFix to deploy a new remote access trojan (RAT) similar to CNCMachineRMS. It allows spying and PC control. Affected users are targeted via malware delivery. Mitigation involves updating systems and monitoring for unauthorized access.

Hackers used 41 AI-assisted PowerShell modules to search for credentials and test API access at an unnamed African stock exchange. Six persistence implants linked to Witchetty, a China-linked espionage group, were found. Indicators of compromise included DNS queries and unusual web server activity. Security teams should monitor DNS logs and compare them with endpoint and authentication logs for signs of intrusion.
title: Hackers Deploy AI-Assisted PowerShell Toolkit to Target African Stock Exchange
Wireshark 4.6.10 Released With Patch for 39 Security Vulnerabilities
content: Wireshark 4.6.10 addresses 39 security vulnerabilities, including crashes, processing loops, memory leaks, and heap disclosures affecting protocol dissectors and capture file parsers. Teams should update to mitigate risks, especially where external capture files are analyzed.

title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day to Gain Admin Access and Steal Data
content: Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8) in VMware vCenter Server, gaining admin access and stealing data. Affects VMware vCenter users. Mitigation: Apply patches immediately.

title: Hackers Leak Customer Data Linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan After Third-Party Cyberattacks
content: Hackers published customer data from third-party service providers linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan. No breaches occurred at the financial companies themselves. The data exposure included names, email addresses, and other marketing details, potentially impacting thousands of customers. Companies are investigating vendor breaches and offering support.

A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock allows physical access users to run programs on a locked Windows PC without signing in, gaining only limited account access. The method was posted by researchers MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, impacting Windows systems until a patch is applied.
title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It

content: Drupal released updates to fix a critical RCE flaw, enabling unauthenticated attackers to take over vulnerable sites. The installer bug affects Drupal core versions and could lead to remote code execution. Administrators must update to the latest version to mitigate risk.
title: Drupal Fixes Critical RCE Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated Takeover

content: KPMG Canada confirmed a cybersecurity breach where confidential tax documents of some clients were accessed. Immediate actions included containment and communication with affected clients. The nature and extent of the breach remain unclear, as details on the type of data accessed are not disclosed. Clients should verify information and monitor their accounts for unusual activity.
title: KPMG Canada Confirms Cyberattack as Hackers Access Confidential Client Tax Documents
Critical Zero-Day in Windows Package Manager Exposes Microsoft’s Software Supply Chain
content: A zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft’s Windows Package Manager (WinGet) allowed a single pull request to potentially compromise moderator credentials, exposing a significant supply chain risk. The flaw, present in the internal triage tool, could allow attackers to access and modify Microsoft repositories, including pushing backdoored installers. Microsoft has patched the vulnerability, but the underlying credential model is criticized as fundamentally flawed. Enterprises must review their automation tools and replace broad, long-lived tokens with narrow, short-lived ones to mitigate similar risks.

title: 8.8 Million NGINX Services Potentially Exposed to Critical NGINX2Root Vulnerability
content: Around 8.8 million NGINX services may still be exposed to a critical set of five memory bugs. These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated remote users to run commands as the NGINX worker process. The most severe bug, CVE-2026-123007, affects all NGINX versions from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8. Patching or disabling HTTP/2 is recommended to mitigate the risk. No exploitation has been reported in the wild as of 18 November 2026.

title: Hackers Exploit VMware vCenter 0-Day Since September to Hijack Admin Accounts and Steal VM Data
content: A suspected China-linked espionage group exploited a VMware vCenter Server zero-day in September 2026, gaining admin access and stealing files from a Windows VM. The group used custom tools and stole encryption material and database credentials. Patching is required, but does not fully mitigate the threat.

title: European Commission HR systems hit by cyber attack using ARTEX tool
content: The European Commission HR systems were compromised by attackers using the ARTEX penetration testing tool. The attack forced the Commission to temporarily shut down access for over 10 days. No evidence of a data breach was found, but the attackers are suspected to have searched for and located credentials. HR systems, containing sensitive information, were targeted, making them a valuable prize for espionage and social engineering. Mitigation includes checking other systems and defining secure fallback processes.

A newly disclosed Windows 11 zero-day called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access bypass parts of the Windows lock screen and run code without signing in, potentially exposing a running PC even when BitLocker is enabled. The issue affects Narrator and requires at least one user account linked to an online Microsoft account. Microsoft has not issued a patch as of the reporting date. Teams should limit physical access to exposed devices and watch for an advisory.
title: New Windows 11 Narrator Lock Screen 0-Day Allows Attackers to Bypass BitLocker Protections
VMware and KVM Vulnerabilities Require Urgent Attention
content: VMware published critical advisories for two vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123890 and CVE-2026-123891) in vCenter and SDDC Manager, allowing unauthorized access and command execution. Additionally, KVM has a CVE-2026-99312 that enables DoS and memory corruption attacks on hosts with AMD processors. Mitigation involves applying patches and disabling nested virtualization where applicable.

title: Germ Network Launches Android Version of Encrypted Messaging App
content: Germ Network, a new encrypted messaging client, launched its Android version, seeing a 20x jump in usage since its iOS release. The app uses end-to-end encryption and a unique card system for identity management, aiming to provide more control over shared information. Collaboration with Bluesky and AT Protocol supports its growth, but Germ plans to introduce premium features later. Security and privacy are top concerns, with efforts to minimize metadata and avoid AI integration risks.

title: AWS re:Invent 2026 Security and Governance Sessions
content: AWS invites attendees to re:Invent 2026 for security, identity, and governance sessions. Focused on themes like securing agentic enterprises and building security for rapid development, these sessions aim to equip professionals with tools and best practices for modern cloud security. Attendees can participate in keynotes, workshops, and breakout sessions covering a wide range of security domains.

Technical segments on setting up Waydroid and Mitmproxy. Security news includes AI in pentesting, RCE vulnerabilities, and surveillance through ad tech. Mitigation involves staying informed and addressing emerging threats.
title: Security Weekly Episode 953: Technical Segments and Security News
OpenSSF Global Cyber Policy Working Group Workshop at Open Source Summit Europe
content: The OpenSSF Global Cyber Policy Working Group held a workshop at Open Source Summit Europe to discuss cybersecurity policy, focusing on due diligence, vulnerability reporting, and collaboration between manufacturers and maintainers. The sessions highlighted challenges in implementing the Cyber Resilience Act, particularly around due diligence and vulnerability reporting. The group plans to provide more practical guidance and tools to address these issues.

title: AWS Introduces Security Analytics Dashboard for AWS WAF
content: AWS has introduced a new security analytics dashboard for AWS WAF to help security teams investigate traffic, identify threats, and reduce false positives. It provides a global view of blocked requests across protection packs, domains, and regions, and allows filtering by various dimensions like IP addresses, user-agent, and more. This dashboard helps in investigating traffic spikes and tuning rules to reduce false positives.

title: Critical flaw in VMware vCenter allows authentication bypass
content: A severe authentication bypass vulnerability in VMware vCenter (CVE-2026-123890) allows unauthorized access. Patches are available for vCenter versions 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, and 8.0 U3m. Other vulnerabilities, including SQL-injection and command-injection flaws, also exist but have lower severity. Immediate patching is advised to mitigate risks.

title: Supply Chain Compromise via Malicious Third-Party JavaScript
content: Visitors to websites of major brands were served malicious JavaScript through a compromised third-party web service. The attack did not breach individual sites but used a vendor’s platform weakness to inject malicious code. Affected organizations lost payment card details, cryptocurrency, and session cookies. Mitigation includes strict Content Security Policy, inventory of third-party scripts, and continuous monitoring.

Visitors to websites of major brands were served malicious JavaScript through a compromised third-party web service. The attack exploited a weakness in the vendor’s platform, allowing attackers to modify customer-delivered scripts, which were then served to all visitors. This affected banks, airlines, and software companies. The attack stole payment card details and tampered with cryptocurrency transactions. Mitigation includes a strict Content Security Policy and inventorying third-party scripts.
title: Malicious JavaScript Injected Through Trustworthy Third-Party CDN in Supply Chain Attack

content: Third-party breaches at JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard may have exposed customer names and email addresses. No impact on payments data or services. Financial firms are investigating incidents but details on specific data stolen and third-party providers are limited.
title: Chase, Visa, Mastercard confirm third-party cyberattacks potentially exposing customer information

content: This week, social engineering techniques are being used to steal data and spread malware via familiar objects and services. AI is enhancing attackers' capabilities.
title: ThreatsDay: GPT-6.2 Jailbreak Flaws, BubbleLoader PNG Malware, $500M Ransom Demands + 17 More Stories

content: A Russian national stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company assisting Ukraine. He photographed employees, tracked their movements, and collected home addresses. The actions left one employee in emotional distress, prompting a 911 call. Mitigation involves heightened security and employee awareness.
title: Russian National Indicted for Spying on Silicon Valley Tech and Defense Firm
Drupal Core Vulnerabilities Exploited (AV26-1186)
content: Drupal core versions prior to 10.6.22, 11.3.22, and 11.4.13 are affected by vulnerabilities, including a critical remote code execution flaw. Users and administrators are advised to update to the latest versions immediately to mitigate risks.

AWS Security Incident Response continuously evaluates threat findings from Amazon GuardDuty and Security Hub to triage and manage security incidents. Most findings are archived if deemed benign, while suspicious activities trigger proactive cases. This process helps teams focus on confirmed threats, reducing alert volume and improving response efficiency.
title: AWS Security Incident Response Process Overview

content: VMware products, including vCenter and Cloud Foundation, are affected by vulnerabilities exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-123890 is actively used, impacting versions prior to 9.1.1.0200, 8.0 U3m, and 5.2.5. CISA added the vulnerability to their KEV database. Users are advised to apply updates to mitigate risks.
title: VMware Security Advisory (AV26-1185) – Update 1
Nvidia investigates alleged data breach by ransomware group The Gentlemen's affiliates
content: Nvidia is investigating a possible data breach following claims by The Gentlemen's ransomware group that they stole sensitive information. While Nvidia has not found evidence of system involvement, the group is known for prolific attacks. The actual number of victims may be higher, given Check Point's findings of over 1,570 compromised entities.

title: Mitel Security Advisory AV26-1184
content: Mitel reported vulnerabilities in MiCollab versions prior to or equal to 10.3 (10.3.0.18). Users are advised to apply the necessary updates. Affected are Mitel users and administrators.

title: PHP Group security advisory (AV26-1183)
content: PHP Group identified vulnerabilities in versions prior to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, and 8.5.13, and 8.6.0. Users and administrators are advised to update their systems to the latest versions to mitigate the risks.

title: Ubiquiti Security Advisory (AV26-1182)
content: Ubiquiti's UniFi Access Application (prior to 4.3.24) is affected by vulnerabilities. Users and administrators are advised to review the provided web link and apply necessary updates to mitigate risks.

title: JetBrains Security Advisory (AV26-1181)
content: JetBrains products, particularly TeamCity versions prior to 2026.2.1 and 2026.1.5, are affected by vulnerabilities. Users are advised to review and apply necessary updates. Technical impact includes potential exploitation, while mitigation involves applying available patches.

title: CraftCMS Security Advisory (AV26-1180)
content: CraftCMS versions prior to 5.11.5 are affected by vulnerabilities. Users and administrators are advised to review and apply necessary updates.

title: FBI Targets Ransomware Scammers in Undercover Operation
content: FBI posed as ransomware victim and attacker to target Florida-based company run by Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar. The company claimed to offer data recovery services. No clear technical impact or mitigation provided.

A fake Tesla livestream using a deepfake of Elon Musk tricked Coinbase users into sending $4.7 million in crypto. The scam relied on convincing viewers to send funds to a fake address. Automated defenses prevented most transfers. To avoid such scams, be wary of offers too good to be true, avoid sending crypto to addresses in videos, and verify offers on official websites.
title: Deepfake Elon Musk scam nearly costs viewers $4.7 million in crypto
Fake Elon Musk Livestream Scam Nearly Costs Viewers $4.7 Million in Crypto
content: A deepfake Elon Musk livestream tricked Coinbase users into sending over $4.7 million in crypto. The scam, which did not break into accounts, instead convinced users to send funds. Automated defenses stopped most transfers. To avoid: be wary of deals too good to be true, verify requests, and avoid clicking on links in videos or messages.

Multiple vulnerabilities in NGINX could allow remote code execution. Affected is web serving, reverse proxying, caching, and load balancing software. Exploitation could lead to full system access. Mitigation involves updating to patched versions or configuring less privileged accounts.
title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in NGINX Could Allow for Remote Code Execution

content: A vulnerability in PHP's session storage can be exploited to execute code. The flaw, phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714), allows attackers to manipulate session writes and run arbitrary code on the server. Affected users should update to the latest PHP releases for mitigation.
title: PHP's session storage flaw exploited for code execution

content: A new PHP attack, phpAfterShell, bypasses October patches for PHP2Shell, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability affects servers using PHP’s default file-based session handler. Applications storing sessions in Redis or a database are unaffected. Patched releases include PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, and 8.5.13. Mitigation involves disabling session upload progress or upgrading to a supported PHP version.
title: New phpAfterShell Attack Bypasses PHP2Shell Fix to Enable Remote Code Execution

content: VMware vCenter and SDDC Manager have multiple vulnerabilities, allowing remote attackers to bypass authentication and gain full control. The most critical flaw, CVE-2026-123890, enables unauthenticated access. Affected systems include vCenter, SDDC Manager, and VMware Tools. Patching is essential to mitigate risks. Admins should update to the latest versions and review access controls and logs.
title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaws Let Hackers Bypass Authentication and Access Servers

content: A cyberattack targeted third-party vendors providing services to JPMorgan Chase, potentially exposing customer names and email addresses. The bank did not specify how many customers were affected or confirm the extent of data exposure. JPMorgan Chase plans to notify affected customers and offer free credit monitoring.
title: JPMorgan Chase Confirms Third-Party Cyberattack That May Have Exposed Customer Names and Emails

content: Attackers are targeting AI agents in company computers, using plain text prompts to find secrets and send information externally. Security teams need to monitor AI tool permissions, instruction sources, and actions. Kaspersky recommends using familiar tools like application control, web filtering, EDR, and up-to-date threat intelligence. Key measures include creating an approved AI app registry, restricting access, and monitoring launch parameters and file access.
title: Protecting Companies from AI-Driven Cyber Attacks
Russian National Indicted for Spying on US Defense Tech Company
content: A Russian national, Igor D'iu, was indicted for spying on a US defense tech company in Palo Alto, allegedly following employees, taking photos of their screens, and leaving remote surveillance devices. FBI agents claim he received instructions via Telegram, suggesting involvement of Russian intelligence. The indicted individual faces charges of espionage and possession of fake IDs.
OpenVPN 2.7.8 and earlier versions are affected by a vulnerability. The Cyber Centre advises users and administrators to review the provided web links and apply necessary updates.
title: OpenVPN Security Advisory (AV26-1179)

content: AptDeco, a high-end furniture marketplace, is facing complaints from sellers who have not been paid after selling items on the platform. Sellers report delayed payments and vague updates from customer service, while AptDeco attributes delays to technical issues. The company is facing legal issues and potential class action lawsuits.
title: High-End Furniture Marketplace AptDeco Faces Seller Payment Delays and Complaints
F5 Security Advisory (AV26-1178)
content: F5 Network products, including BIG-IP, BIG-IP APM, BIG-IP SSL Orchestrator, BIG-IP PEM, BIG-IP CNF, BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes, and BIG-IQ Centralized Management, are affected by multiple vulnerabilities. Users and administrators are advised to review and apply necessary updates as available.

Proton Drive introduces Easy Switch for Google Drive, allowing direct file and folder transfers. The feature is available on all plans, including free. This enhances user migration between cloud storage services.
title: Proton Drive Adds Direct ‘Easy Switch’ Imports from Google Drive

content: Google is retaining Gemini conversations for two months even when chat history is disabled. This affects both temporary chats and those started with history off. The update impacts user data retention policies globally.
title: Google extends retention of Gemini chat data
Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
content: A zero-day flaw in VMware vCenter allows network attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Affects vCenter management of ESX hosts and virtual machines. Fixed versions are available, but no workaround is provided.

title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
content: Ransomware attacks involve credential theft, lateral movement, and disabling security controls. Acronis highlights five warning signs to detect intrusions early and protect systems. This helps in containing malicious activity and safeguarding critical data.

Criminal IP launched AITEM, combining asset discovery with AI-assisted investigation and dark web monitoring. It helps teams understand exposure and prioritize actions. Organizations can use it to assess and validate security risks in their web assets.
title: Criminal IP Launches AITEM for AI-Powered Asset Discovery and Exposure Management

content: The PHP Foundation released security updates to fix 7 critical flaws, including remote code execution vulnerabilities. Affected deployments must apply the patches promptly to mitigate risks.
title: PHP Addresses Multiple Critical Security Flaws
Study Reveals Racial Disparities in Data Center Location
content: A study found that data centers are more likely to be built in Black, Hispanic, and Asian neighborhoods, exacerbating racial disparities. Researchers examined 81,000 US census tracts and 5,291 data centers, noting the historical legacy of redlining and its impact on infrastructure. The study suggests zoning regulations and prioritizing racial equity in data center construction to mitigate these issues.

A security breach compromised account details of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers in Transport for London (TfL). The portal was taken offline, and the incident is contained. TfL discovered the issue on November 16, 2026.
title: TfL breach exposed data of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers

content: Drupal core has a critical vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to reinstall sites and potentially execute remote code. Fixed releases for all supported branches were issued. Affected are Drupal sites using the installer feature under specific conditions.
title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw for Unauthenticated Attacks

content: ICE is paying AT&T to analyze trillions of phone records and location data. The program potentially affects AT&T customers and non-customers alike. Experts raise concerns about mass surveillance and lack of judicial oversight.
title: ICE Pays AT&T for Access to Massive Phone Records
PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Urges Users to Update
content: PHP announced critical security vulnerabilities affecting all supported versions, urging users to update promptly. The flaws, including remote code execution and use-after-free issues, require non-default settings or uncommon setups. Administrators should patch their installations, check the PHP changelog, and restart workers post-update. PHP 8.2 will end support on December 31, 2026.

title: Meta AI Agent Muse Reads Encrypted Messages Through Android Notifications and Mac Permissions
content: Meta’s AI agent Muse can read Signal messages on Android and Macs via notification and accessibility permissions, highlighting potential privacy risks. Users should review app permissions and adjust settings to mitigate risks.

title: BADBOX 3.0 Malware Infects Android TV Boxes for Ad Fraud
content: BADBOX 3.0 malware infects low-cost Android TV boxes, generating 40 billion fraudulent ad requests daily. The malware, disguised as a system app, downloads additional modules for ad fraud and residential proxy enrollment. Affected boxes primarily run Android Open Source Project (AOSP) and are not Play Protect certified. Mitigation includes disconnecting suspicious devices from the network and verifying Play Protect certification before purchase.

Russian hackers stole login credentials for US banks, IRS, and Social Security from infected Windows PCs using a Python implant. The malware broke browser encryption to access saved passwords and cookies, even from password managers and MFA. The attackers obtained 3,345 passwords and 30 cookie databases from 16 victims. Security teams should monitor for pythonw.exe files and block certain IP addresses and domains.
title: Russian Hackers Steal US Bank, IRS, and Social Security Login Credentials
Charting American Culture in News Footage of ‘Grand Theft Auto’
content: The article discusses the cultural impact and media coverage of the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) video game series over two decades, from 2001 to 2026. It highlights how the initial concerns about violence and sexual content have shifted to concerns about the game's economic impact on the industry and society. This shift in focus reflects broader cultural changes and anxieties. The media's coverage has evolved from moral panics to business-oriented discussions, illustrating the changing cultural perceptions of video games.

Google released Chrome 158, fixing 204 security issues, including six critical flaws. Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge used AI to discover two of the critical vulnerabilities. Users should update to the latest version to mitigate risks. The update addresses memory-safety errors, graphics-related vulnerabilities, and more.
title: Chrome 158 Patches Six Critical Flaws, Two Found with AI’s Help

content: CISA added four flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog after finding evidence of active exploitation. Affected products include Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap. Mitigation involves updating to the latest supported releases and checking for pre-patch compromise. Federal civilian agencies face patch deadlines from Nov 21 to Dec 2.
title: CISA Warns Hackers Are Actively Exploiting Four Flaws in Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and REDCap

content: Google released Chrome 158 with 204 security fixes, six critical. AI-assisted by Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge, two critical flaws found. Update Chrome to protect against potential memory corruption and execution of malicious code.
title: Chrome 158 patches six critical flaws, two found with AI

content: A Russian national was indicted for allegedly using remote access software and following employees to spy on a Silicon Valley technology and defense firm. The operation aimed to gather information about employees and their home addresses, involving unauthorized surveillance and potential stalking. The case highlights the threat of cyber espionage targeting defense firms.
title: Russian National Accused of Using Remote Access Tools to Spy on Silicon Valley Defense Firm

content: Attackers exploited PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) in firewall management interfaces, allowing unauthorized code execution. Affected were firewalls with exposed PAN-OS interfaces. Mitigation involves patching and securing management access.
title: PHP2Shell Exploits Firewall Vulnerabilities

content: Hackers use fake payment notices and SharePoint documents to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts through device code phishing. This technique bypasses multifactor authentication by tricking employees into authorizing sessions they did not initiate. Security teams should filter sign-in logs for device code flow and block unauthorized access. Indicators of compromise include suspicious domains and URLs.
title: Hackers Exploit Microsoft 365 Device Code Authentication to Hijack Accounts and Bypass MFA
Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions
content: A data breach at software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details at 40 Irish credit unions. The breach, discovered in October, impacted credit unions' online banking platforms, exposing names, BICs, and IBANs. Wellington IT notified affected credit unions after a delay, and the company is investigating the incident. Credit union members were advised not to transfer funds based on false claims.

Palo Alto Networks acquired Applied Compute for $4.5B to integrate AI models into its security offerings. The deal aims to help enterprises securely adopt AI in public or sovereign environments. Palo Alto plans to build its own compute capacity and include model-agnostic protection. CIOs should ensure terms and exit strategies are clear before integrating new models.
title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires Applied Compute for $4.5B to Secure Open-Weight AI Models

content: Recent IT outages at Microsoft, FAA, JPMorgan Chase, and United Airlines raised concerns about potential cyberattacks. However, no evidence linked these disruptions, suggesting they were accidental. Cybersecurity analysts must discern whether such failures are due to technical issues or malicious cyber activities.
title: Determining Cyberattacks Amidst Technological Failures
Hackers Use aNotepad as Malware Delivery Channel for XenoRAT and NodeLinkRAT Backdoors
content: A North Korea-linked hacking group used aNotepad to deploy XenoRAT and NodeLinkRAT backdoors. The campaign targeted South Korean policy and security professionals via spearphishing. The attackers edited a public note page to swap malware, evading detection. They stole documents, account details, and executed commands remotely. Defenders should watch for LNK files, scheduled tasks, and public note page executions.

title: TfL Compromises Oyster Photocard Customer Accounts
content: Transport for London (TfL) experienced a data breach compromising account details of 265,000 Oyster photocard customers, including emails and security questions. No passwords, bank details, or payment card information were compromised. TfL advised customers to change their passwords and security questions. The breach also affected holders of Zip Oyster cards issued to children as young as five. TfL took the website offline for investigation and notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).

N-able confirmed unauthorized access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud environment, disabling management access across regions. Email filtering remained operational, but API and dashboard access were lost. The company is investigating the breach, with no evidence of customer data compromise.
title: N-able Confirms Server Breach, Disables Management Access
Ubiquiti Warns of Critical UniFi Access Flaws Enabling Root Code Execution Attacks
content: Ubiquiti disclosed seven vulnerabilities in its UniFi Access Application, including a critical flaw allowing root code execution. Five rated critical, impacting host and adopted devices. Mitigation: Update to version 4.3.24 or later. Network restrictions reduce exposure but do not replace updates.

title: Sticky note exposure leads to full company network access and sensitive data compromise
content: A password written on a sticky note was used to gain unauthorized access to a company's network, leading to exposure of personal and financial data. The attacker accessed HR and accounting servers, obtaining employee and client information. The company quickly disabled affected accounts, reviewed logs, and tightened access controls.

title: Hackers breach N-able cloud server, disrupting email security management
content: Threat actors gained unauthorized access to N-able's Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, disabling management interfaces and APIs. Affected regions: 3. Mitigation steps are being taken, but investigation is ongoing.

title: CISA Warns of Four Exploited Flaws Linked to Ransomware, Cryptomining, and LLMjacking Attacks
content: CISA warns of four exploited vulnerabilities impacting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt REDCap, linked to ransomware, cryptomining, and LLMjacking. These vulnerabilities are actively exploited.

title: Hackers Target European Commission with ARTEX AI Tool in Major Cyberattack
content: A cyberattack disrupted European Commission staff services for over 10 days. Hackers used ARTEX, an AI tool for finding security weaknesses, to target several applications. The exact extent of data exposure remains unclear, as the Commission did not confirm any data theft. Sysper, MyPMO, and Translation Services were affected. The Commission took security measures and briefed top officials, but the full impact is still under investigation.

title: Scattered Spider’s Phishing and SIM-Swap Tactics Result in Six-Year Sentence
content: Scattered Spider used phishing and SIM-swap techniques to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency from at least 12 companies over six years. Tyler Robert Buchanan, a 24-year-old British man, was sentenced to six years in prison. SIM swapping allowed the group to take over cryptocurrency accounts. Mitigation includes using authenticator apps and being cautious with phone number transfers.

title: Scattered Spider's Phishing and SIM-Swap Tactics Result in Six-Year Sentence
content: Scattered Spider used phishing texts and SIM swaps to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. Tyler Robert Buchanan, a 24-year-old British man, was sentenced to six years in prison. The group targeted companies and individuals, using smishing and SIM swapping to gain access to accounts and steal funds. Mitigation includes using authenticator apps and being cautious with phone number transfers.

title: Cybersecurity Focus Shifts from Vulnerability Management to Remediation
content: The cybersecurity industry's emphasis on identifying and prioritizing vulnerabilities has overlooked the critical step of remediation. Organizations struggle with executing timely and effective fixes, leading to growing vulnerability backlogs and increased exposure. AI-driven vulnerability discovery will exacerbate these issues, necessitating a reevaluation of management processes and governance structures to ensure vulnerabilities are effectively addressed.

title: Hackers Deploy Overlord RAT That Survives Windows Resets and Crashes Systems When Terminated
content: A financially motivated hacking group is deploying Overlord RAT, a Windows remote access trojan that can return after a victim uses ‘Reset this PC.’ The malware can also trigger a blue screen if a user or security tool forcibly ends its process. The campaign targets cryptocurrency holders, gaming account owners, and users of internet calling software. Overlord uses two persistence methods: adding a startup entry to the Windows registry and tampering with the Windows Recovery Environment. The malware retrieves encrypted server addresses from Solana transaction memos and can steal browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and selected documents. Indicators of compromise include staging servers and command-and-control traffic.
Ruby patched seven memory-safety flaws, five of which can trigger remote code execution. Affected are default Rails apps. Mitigation: Update to fixed versions.
title: Ruby Fixes Seven Memory-Safety Flaws, Including Critical Ruby2Shell

content: A critical memory corruption flaw in Ruby’s string case conversion code allows remote code execution (RCE). Affects Ruby 3.3.0-3.3.13, 3.4.0-3.4.12, and 4.0.0-4.0.9. Exploitation can occur in untrusted text processing of legacy encodings. Mitigation: Update to fixed Ruby releases or move to supported branches.
title: Critical One-Byte Heap Overflow in Ruby Could Allow RCE Attacks
Ruby Releases Patches for Seven Security Vulnerabilities, Including RCE Flaws
content: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13, and 3.3.14 were released to fix seven security vulnerabilities, including buffer overflows and RCE flaws in the regular expression engine and string case-conversion code. Affected versions are Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 through 3.4.12, and 4.0.0 through 4.0.9. Users are advised to upgrade and rebuild container images, redeploy services, and verify patched versions to mitigate the risk of remote code execution.

title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
content: A researcher demonstrated memory-corruption bugs in SQL engines, allowing low-privilege database accounts to execute code on the server. Exploits published for PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and Oracle. Mitigation: Update to patched versions.

Splunk released security updates to fix critical remote code execution and authentication bypass vulnerabilities in Splunk SOAR and Enterprise. CVE-2026-131253 allows RCE in the App Wizard, while CVE-2026-76535 lets unauthenticated users run searches under another user’s identity. Administrators should upgrade to version 8.8.0 or later to mitigate risks and verify that key searches and playbooks still function correctly.
title: Splunk Releases Security Updates for SOAR and Enterprise to Patch Critical Flaws

content: Chinese cyberespionage group upgraded EggStreme malware with a silent backdoor to evade detection, targeting government organizations in the Philippines and Taiwan. Newer samples include a passive Windows backdoor and expanded command set. Defenders should monitor DLL sideloading, unmanaged device access, and internal file-share activity.
title: Chinese Hackers Upgrade EggStreme Malware with Silent Backdoor

content: Discussion on a free speech case where the US government agreed to stop pressuring social media platforms and a copyright incident targeting an independent artist. No technical impact or mitigation reported.
title: Free Speech Case and Copyright Incident

content: The U.S. government approved the Secure SI by Design Consortium, led by Palo Alto Networks, to export full-stack SI solutions with embedded cybersecurity. This validation supports sustainable global SI deployment by integrating security from design to runtime, providing government advocacy and export licensing benefits. Enterprises can now scale rapidly while maintaining rigorous security standards.
title: Secure SI by Design Consortium Officially Approved by U.S. Government
Follow-up on Social Engineering Scams and Phishing Schemes
content: This article discusses social engineering scams, phishing schemes, and criminal exploits. Topics include a listener’s question on secure email use, arrests for an AI-powered deepfake CEO impersonation scam, research linking sleep deprivation to increased phishing link clicks, and holiday scam predictions. A listener shares experiences with fake job assessments, while a Reddit post questions a TikTok artist's offer.

Hackers are exploiting a critical RCE vulnerability in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. The flaw, CVE-2026-129448, allows remote code execution without authentication. Administrators should upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later. Affected teams must check and patch their deployments to mitigate the risk.
title: Hackers Actively Exploit Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw to Execute Code Without Authentication

content: PHP released an advisory for critical security flaws in all supported versions. The patch is scheduled for November 19, 2026, between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC. Impacts include potential vulnerabilities, requiring immediate attention to prevent exploitation.
title: PHP Announces Critical Security Flaws and Upcoming Patch

content: AuditTeam, a ransomware group, poses as security auditors, deploying malware and disabling EDR processes with signed antivirus drivers. They encrypted files and demanded a ‘consulting fee’ in addition to a ransom note. The campaign affected multiple organizations globally, targeting security tools and remote access services. Mitigation includes monitoring for new driver installs and limiting local admin rights.
title: AuditTeam Ransomware Gang Uses Security Audit Disguise to Deploy Malware and Kill EDR Processes
What does it take to deploy 200 AI agents safely?
content: AMN Healthcare's CISO faced challenges scaling governance for 200 AI agents. Initial success with 12 agents turned into management struggles as deployment increased. No clear technical incident or breach reported.

title: Hackers Exploit CyberPower UPS Software to Gain SYSTEM Access and Steal Active Directory Data
content: Hackers exploited CyberPower PowerPanel Business software to gain SYSTEM-level access and steal Active Directory data. The attackers used a built-in scripting feature to copy the database and run malware. Symantec recommends limiting access and reviewing settings to prevent similar incidents.

title: Regulatory Changes for AI Cyber Incidents and Export Controls
content: The Trump administration's AI task force encourages leniency in regulatory actions for AI-powered cyber incidents to encourage voluntary reporting. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security tightens controls on AI chip exports to China, but faces challenges in enforcement.

title: Hackers Exploiting Java4Shell RCE Flaw Using ARTEX Disguise Themselves as Chrome
content: Hackers are exploiting Java4Shell RCE flaw by disguising as Chrome traffic. The exploit was detected using Cloudforce One's Cloudforce One, which identified the same IP address scanning and later exploiting targets. The Java4Shell flaw affects OpenJDK’s HotSpot runtime and requires specific conditions to execute. Administrators should apply patches and verify Java versions after updates.

title: WordPress 7.1.5 Addresses 20 Security Issues, Including Potential RCE and SQL Injection Flaws
content: WordPress 7.1.5 was released to address 20 security issues, including potential RCE and SQL injection flaws. The update fixes vulnerabilities in Core, affecting unauthenticated users, administrators, and comments. Immediate updates are recommended to mitigate risks.

The PHP security team plans to release critical updates on November 19, 2026, addressing remote code execution flaws. Users are advised to prepare and install the updates promptly. The CVE-2026-115560 flaw affects session upload progress, while October’s PHP2Shell attacks exploited CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated 9.2 out of 10. Administrators should check and update their PHP versions to mitigate risks.
title: PHP Security Team Warns of Critical Vulnerabilities, Urges Users to Prepare for November 19 Updates

content: Podcast discusses how AI models can be covertly altered to exploit data, emphasizing the importance of monitoring and control over AI usage to prevent data leaks. Companies need to be vigilant about AI tools their staff use.
title: Smashing Security podcast #493: AI model as sleeper agent

content: A heap overflow in Java’s Base64 decoder allows unauthenticated remote code execution only on x86-64 processors with specific AVX-512 features. Affected systems include Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak. Patch all Java runtimes, but prioritize those on processors with all four features. CISA urges immediate patching.
title: Java4Shell: Patch Java, But Check the Processor First

content: Nginx, powering over a third of the internet, faced multiple critical vulnerabilities, including remote code execution and use-after-free, affecting millions of websites for over a decade. AI-assisted researchers found these flaws, leading to an ‘internet breaker’ exploit chain that could lead to root access. F5 patched and recommended immediate updates. Exploitation is complex but potential impacts are severe.
title: AI-Discovered Critical Flaws Expose Millions of Nginx Servers

content: PHP Foundation released multiple security patches, including a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw, affecting all supported versions. Users are advised to upgrade promptly. Earlier critical vulnerabilities, PHP2Shell, were exploited by suspected Chinese attackers for privilege escalation.
title: PHP Foundation releases critical security patches

content: This article details how AWS Security Hub integrates with Azure to provide holistic, multicloud visibility into security risks. It addresses the challenge of prioritizing cross-cloud attacks by correlating findings from both clouds into a single console, enabling analysts to prioritize and respond to threats more effectively. The integration covers identity exposures, initial access, and sensitive data objectives, using MITRE ATT&CK techniques for detailed risk assessment.
title: Detecting cross-cloud lateral movement with AWS Security Hub

content: Recent technology disruptions have led to speculation that outages are attacks. Real outages and attacks can cause similar errors, making it hard to distinguish between them. Social media amplifies this speculation, leading to widespread concerns. Companies and reporters should provide clear explanations and avoid linking unrelated events. Mitigation includes keeping software updated and being cautious about sharing speculative information.
title: Outage or Attack? The Role of Speculation and Social Media in Cybersecurity
Outage or Attack? Don’t Let Social Media Fill in the Gaps
content: Technical failures and cyberattacks can produce similar error messages. Recent disruptions, like Microsoft and FAA outages, often mix with exaggerated reports and conspiracy theories on social media, causing confusion. Companies and media should provide clear explanations and context to avoid panic.

title: Critical Java Flaw and Ongoing Cyberattack
content: A critical Java flaw is exploited, and Equinor confirms an ongoing cyberattack. Oracle patches 655 vulnerabilities. Scattered Spider leader faces legal consequences for crypto thefts.

F5 released emergency patches for 10 critical remote code execution flaws in NGINX, affecting 225M websites. AI-assisted researchers found bugs that could be exploited for data theft and service disruption. Immediate updates are advised.
title: AI-Discovered Vulnerabilities in NGINX Threaten Millions of Websites
SmarterTools Security Advisory (AV26-1177)
content: SmarterTools products, specifically SmarterMail prior to Build 9817, are affected by vulnerabilities. Users are advised to review and apply updates as available.

JetBrains products, specifically TeamCity versions prior to 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, are affected by vulnerabilities. Users are advised to review and apply necessary updates to mitigate potential exploits.
title: JetBrains Security Advisory: AV26-1176

content: A critical Java vulnerability, Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), allows unauthenticated attackers to read Java heap memory, steal private keys, tokens, and session secrets, and achieve remote code execution. The vulnerability impacts all Java instances using AVX-512 VBMI instructions. Enterprises struggle with visibility and patching due to Java's ubiquity and hidden nature. Mitigation requires comprehensive inventory and patching across vendors and versions.
title: Java4Shell Exploit Leverages Memory Corruption to Steal Sensitive Data and Achieve Remote Code Execution

content: Cisco has issued a security advisory for vulnerabilities in Secure Endpoint Connectors for Linux, Mac, and Windows, prior to versions 1.29.3, 1.27.5, and 8.6.4, respectively. Users are advised to review and apply necessary updates.
title: Cisco Security Advisory for Vulnerable Endpoint Connectors
US Logistics Firms Targeted by Fake FMCSA, DAT, and TIMOCOM Portals
content: Attackers impersonate carrier-verification, broker-onboarding, and load-board platforms to deploy backdoors and steal credentials. Targets include US trucking and logistics companies through three campaigns: HelloFriends, NodeRemote, and Fake Freight Portals. Mitigation involves verifying requests through official channels, training staff, and monitoring for unauthorized remote management tools.

title: F5 Security Advisory: AV26-1174
content: F5 has issued a security advisory for vulnerabilities in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source versions prior to 37.3.0.1 and 1.31.9, respectively. Users are advised to apply updates to mitigate potential exploits.

title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
content: A decade-old NGINX HTTP/2 flaw enables unauthenticated attackers to execute code on servers. Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 released. Affects servers running HTTP/2. Mitigation: Update to fixed versions immediately.

title: F5 Warns 6 Critical BIG-IP Flaws Can Crash Traffic in Specific Setups, May Allow RCE
content: Six critical vulnerabilities in F5 BIG-IP can crash the Traffic Management Microkernel, disrupting traffic. Specific setups, like iRule commands or APM policies, are required for exploitation. F5 disclosed the flaws, warning of potential Remote Code Execution.

A critical unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability in Apache Roller’s XML-RPC endpoint is actively being exploited. This RCE flaw, CVE-2026-129448, could lead to remote code execution. Affected users should update to the latest version immediately.
title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
Hackers Use GhostMap eBPF Rootkit to Conceal IronWorm Malware
content: Hackers are deploying the GhostMap eBPF rootkit to hide IronWorm malware from Linux security tools. The rootkit obscures processes, files, and network sockets. Aqua Security identified the rootkit in the IronWorm and Atomic Arch payloads. Investigators should compare process listings with execution records and review unexpected services. Indicators of compromise include specific file paths, packages, and hashes.

Hackers are deploying a Linux botnet called Evooo1Bot using hidden cron jobs that reinstall malware every 5 minutes. Affected devices include routers, firewalls, and IP cameras. The malware reuses Mirai code, includes encrypted control traffic, and can act as a SOCKS proxy. Proper cleanup requires removing all startup entries, not just cron jobs. Defenders should check /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d/, and other scheduler files for suspicious activity.
title: Hackers Deploy Malware Using Hidden Cron Jobs on Firewalls and Routers

content: Drupal core contains a chain of methods that could be exploited if an insecure deserialization vulnerability exists. This theoretical issue, not directly exploitable, requires another vulnerability to pass unsafe input. Affected versions range from <10.6.22 to >=11.4.13. Update to the latest versions to mitigate. Reported by the Drupal Security Team.
title: Drupal Core Gadget Chain Vulnerability Exploited

content: Waymo suspended driverless freeway rides in the US after California regulators banned the company from operating on freeways due to incidents involving construction zones and attempts to bypass police. The ban affects areas including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, Phoenix, and Austin. Waymo continues to operate on city streets. Safety concerns include vehicle incursions into construction zones and incidents like blocking traffic and animal deaths.
title: Waymo Suspended Freeway Operations in Multiple US Cities Due to Safety Incidents

content: Drupal core has a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-132165) in install.php. Affected versions are <10.6.22, >=11.0.0 <11.3.22, >=11.4.0 <11.4.13. Exploits were reported on live sites as early as 2026-11-19. Sites should upgrade to the latest version to mitigate risks.
title: Drupal core - Highly critical - Remote code execution - SA-CORE-2026-017
Microsoft’s official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
content: Microsoft’s official agent framework was hijacked to distribute info-stealing malware, targeting nearly 200,000 users. The malware exfiltrates environment variables, credentials, and secrets. It remains active as long as the malicious version is installed. Microsoft has made some repositories private for investigation. Users should update and verify the authenticity of their Python packages.

title: WordPress 7.1.5 Release Addresses Multiple Security Vulnerabilities
content: WordPress 7.1.5 addresses multiple security vulnerabilities including SQL injection, XSS, and information disclosure issues. Affected users are encouraged to update immediately. Technical impact ranges from unauthenticated privilege escalation to SQL injection. Response involves updating to the latest version or manually applying backported fixes.

Microsoft released 1,414 vulnerabilities in October 2026, with one already being exploited. The Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found vulnerability exploitation as the leading breach vector. The AI-ROC, through its AI agents, aims to detect exposures, validate exploitability, and remediate autonomously to close the gap between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation. Security teams can trust the results, with policy controls and approvals.
title: AI-ROC Aims to Bridge the Gap Between Vulnerability Exploitation and Remediation
Microsoft’s Large Patch Tuesday Highlights AI-ROC’s Urgent Need for Vulnerability Management
content: Microsoft released over 1,400 vulnerabilities in two consecutive Patch Tuesdays, with some exploited within hours. CISA set tight deadlines for remediation, underscoring the need for faster vulnerability detection, validation, and remediation. The AI-ROC model aims to address these challenges by automating detection, validation, and remediation, ensuring risks are reduced quickly.

An AI hacking framework, CyberStrikeAI, executed 221 security tools automatically in a single session, highlighting the risks of unvetted AI operations. The session did not involve human approval, raising concerns about potential misuse. Security researchers noted that while the agent's actions were recorded, they lacked evidence of actual breaches. For security teams, this incident underscores the importance of monitoring AI tool approvals and securing conversation databases.
title: AI Hacking Framework CyberStrikeAI Runs 221 Tool Executions Without Human Approval

content: OffSec released over 80 hands-on labs based on real CVEs, including PHPH2Shell, to help security teams understand and defend against newly disclosed vulnerabilities. These labs cover both offensive and defensive aspects, reflecting the growing role of AI in identifying and exploiting security flaws.
title: After Black October, OffSec Turns PHPH2Shell and Other New Vulnerabilities Into Hands-On Labs

content: Two critical vulnerabilities in NGINX enable remote code execution. Affecting sites using HTTP/2, attackers can compromise servers even when applications behind them are secure. Organizations need to update to fixed versions to mitigate risk.
title: NGINX HTTP/2 Flaws Could Allow Memory Corruption and Remote Code Execution on Web Servers
Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
content: Oracle released fixes for a remote code execution vulnerability in OpenJDK (CVE-2026-114938) affecting OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 and later versions on x86-64 platforms. Cisco products using these Java versions are at risk. High severity. Immediate patching recommended.

title: Cyber insurers now want proof you can actually recover
content: Cyber insurance pricing has cooled as insurers impose stricter requirements, focusing on proof of recovery and speed. Backup testing, recovery times, and a clean recovery location are now essential. Insurers prioritize minimizing claim costs and ensuring businesses can recover quickly without reintroducing threats. This shift impacts law firms, healthcare providers, and managed service providers, requiring improved data protection postures.

The 2027 Cybersecurity Excellence Awards launched, introducing six new AI security categories to recognize excellence in AI security post-SPM, red-teaming, and supply chain security. The program invites nominations from cybersecurity companies and professionals worldwide.
title: 2027 Cybersecurity Excellence Awards Launch With Six New AI Security Categories
GNU Security Advisory (AV26-1173)
content: A vulnerability has been identified in Emacs versions prior to 31.2. The GNU Cyber Centre advises users and administrators to review and apply any necessary updates to mitigate the risk.

SpyCloud predicts that attackers will exploit trusted access points such as hijacked sessions, API keys, and vendor connections in 2027. This includes MFA bypass, AI-driven phishing, and stolen non-human identity credentials. The technical impact is significant, with potential for large-scale breaches and fraud. Mitigation involves enhancing visibility into exposed access and automating remediation.
title: SpyCloud’s 2027 Forecast: Attackers Will Exploit Trusted Access, From Hijacked Sessions to AI Agents
ClamAV Vulnerabilities Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
content: Multiple vulnerabilities in ClamAV could allow a remote attacker to bypass security limits and cause a denial of service, impacting Cisco Secure Endpoint Connector for Windows. Cisco has released software updates. The Security Impact Rating is High for Windows and Medium for other platforms.

title: Armornet Launches AI Security Platform for Software Supply Chain
content: Armornet introduces an AI-driven security platform that continuously monitors vendors and software supply chains, addressing the dynamic risk landscape. The platform provides real-time risk scores and integrates with version control, compliance, and workspace tools. This addresses the challenges of static vendor risk assessments and the evolving threat landscape, such as the 75% growth in open-source malware in 2025. Mitigation involves continuously monitoring vendor risk and providing training through open-source cybersecurity games.

AI is enhancing cyberattacks, pushing enterprises to focus on post-incident recovery. Infinidat's InfiniBox and InfiniBox SSA platforms, with InfiniSafe, offer immutable snapshots, logical air-gapping, and AI-based detection to quickly recover critical data. This shifts cybersecurity towards proactive recovery strategies.
title: AI-driven cybersecurity strategies and tools for enterprise recovery

content: OX Security introduces OX Radar and Response Center to monitor and manage cyber threats, helping security teams identify and remediate vulnerabilities and supply chain risks. The solution continuously tracks emerging threats and automatically assesses customer exposure, providing critical information for immediate action.
title: OX Security Launches OX Radar and Response Center for Cyber Threat Monitoring and Management

content: A suspected Chinese APT group uses a new EggStreme malware variant to evade detection and target government organizations in the Philippines. The malware remains silent to avoid exposure, employing frequent recompilation and domain changes to bypass security tools.
title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
GitHub Security Advisory AV26-1172
content: GitHub is affected by vulnerabilities in Enterprise Server versions prior to 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. Users and administrators are advised to review release notes and apply necessary updates.
Attackers use deepfakes, helpdesk impersonation, and fake IT support to deceive employees, gaining unauthorized access. Stronger identity verification can prevent such social engineering threats.
title: From Deepfakes to Helpdesk Impersonation: Why Stronger Verification Matters

content: OX Security introduces OX Radar and Response Center, a platform that monitors critical vulnerabilities and supply chain threats, automatically assessing customer exposure and guiding remediation. The technology continuously tracks emerging threats and provides actionable insights to security teams, reducing manual investigation efforts.
title: OX Security Launches OX Radar and Response Center for Real-Time Cyber Threat Monitoring
Microsoft Releases Windows Server 2028 with Pre-Hardened Security Settings
content: Microsoft released Windows Server 2028 in public preview with hundreds of security settings enabled by default. This change aims to reduce the initial exposure window for new servers. Admins can now start from a hardened setup and relax only what a workload requires. The update includes enhanced identity and authentication, network security, and cryptography. It targets common security issues like weak SMB signing. This release is part of Microsoft's ongoing efforts to improve server security and ease the administrative burden.

title: Oracle November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update
content: Oracle released patches for 655 vulnerabilities, impacting various product families. 9.5% rated critical, 38% important, and 274 medium. Oracle Hyperion received the most patches (267), with 107 remotely exploitable. Critical vulnerabilities include CVE-2026-114880 and CVE-2026-114924. Mitigation: Apply patches promptly to prevent exploitation.

Microsoft’s AI Identifies 99 Security Issues in Open-Source Projects
content: Microsoft and GitHub’s AI identified 99 security issues in six open-source projects, including Express and ImageMagick. Maintainers fixed 55 issues, with 14 making it into software releases. The process highlights AI’s potential in enhancing security research and vulnerability management in open-source communities.

Researchers demonstrated that a Windows Hello PIN can be guessed in 40 hours using cheap hardware, bypassing the 69-day lockout. This exploit also cuts the worst-case time to crack a BitLocker PIN from 19 years to 20 days. The attack targets vulnerabilities in Winbond flash chips and AMD's non-volatile controller, allowing for counter value forgery and rollback. The exploit impacts over a billion Windows 11 devices. Microsoft advises using longer PINs and enhanced Group Policy settings to mitigate risks.
title: New Hello Again Attack Exploits Weaknesses in TPM and BitLocker

title: AI Agent Sues Meta Over Account Suspension
content: Joe Thomas, an epoxy countertop business owner, used Meta’s AI agent ‘Baby Mia’ to run his business and marketing. Meta suspended his Facebook pages, accusing Baby Mia of being a hacker. Scammers Use Web Push Notifications to Trick Users
content: Scammers use permission requests during quizzes or engaging stories to enable push notifications, allowing them to repeatedly send alarming messages and advertisements. Users are advised to be cautious and use web protection tools to manage permissions and block unwanted notifications.

Evooo1Bot, a Linux botnet, deploys malware using cron jobs that run every five minutes to reinstall the malware. This persistence method ensures the device reinfects itself even after the malware process is terminated. Administrators must inspect and clear scheduled jobs to prevent reinfection.
title: Malware Uses Cron for Persistence on Network Appliances
Scammers Use Browser Push Notifications for Deceptive Advertising and Fraud
content: Scammers exploit browser push notifications to repeatedly target users with ads, fake security alerts, and scams after they leave a deceptive website. This technique allows them to trick users into clicking harmful links or downloading malware. Malwarebytes and HUMAN Security investigations revealed campaigns such as Pushpaganda, which used AI-generated content to lure users into granting notifications permissions. Users are advised to only allow notifications from trusted sites and to use web protection tools.
